name: Kim Ji-yeon
milestone_by_age_26: Won individual sabre gold at the 2012 London Olympics at age 24, becoming the first South Korean woman to win an Olympic fencing gold medal.
early_history_summary: Kim began fencing at age 13 in Busan as a foil fencer before switching to sabre at 16 on coach Lee Soo-geun's advice. She joined the national team at 18 in 2006 but was often overshadowed by other sabre fencers until becoming a fixture in the 2011 season, winning her first international medals that year.
family_context_summary: Born in Busan, South Korea; parents initially opposed her fencing career, with her father unable to attend matches due to work and her mother first watching live only in 2014.
primary_early_advantage_tags: national team pipeline, coach conversion, sabre specialization
evidence_summary: Kim Ji-yeon began fencing at age 13 in Busan, initially as a foil fencer before switching to sabre at 16 on the advice of coach Lee Soo-geun. Her parents initially opposed her fencing career, and she was often overshadowed by other sabre fencers early in her national team career. She joined the national team at 18 in 2006 but didn't become a fixture until 2011, winning her first international medals that year. At the 2012 London Olympics, at age 24, she won individual sabre gold, becoming the first South Korean woman to win an Olympic fencing gold medal.
starting_point: Born in Busan, South Korea to a family with no documented fencing background; parents initially opposed her pursuit of the sport.
current_position: Retired from national team in 2023 after 14-year career; continued competing for Seoul City club; married in 2017.

trajectory.event: Won individual sabre gold at the London Olympics, the first South Korean woman to win Olympic fencing gold.
Won two gold medals at the Incheon Asian Games in individual and team sabre.
Won individual gold medal at the World Fencing Championships.
Won team sabre bronze at the Tokyo Olympics, South Korea's first women's sabre team Olympic medal.
Retired from the national team after 14 consecutive years as a national representative.

name: Saharon Shelah
milestone_by_age_26: Completed PhD on stable theories at Hebrew University in 1969 at age 24, extending Morley's categoricity theorem and laying the foundation for classification theory in model theory; immediately appointed lecturer at Princeton University.
early_history_summary: Shelah decided to become a mathematician at age 15 after discovering geometry, earned his B.Sc. from Tel Aviv University at 19, served in the IDF, and completed his M.Sc. at Hebrew University at 22 before finishing his PhD at 24 under Michael Rabin.
family_context_summary: Born in Jerusalem to Yonatan Ratosh (Uriel Heilperin), a prominent Israeli poet and Canaanite political activist who emigrated from Warsaw in 1921 and studied at the Hebrew University.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a poet and political activist, not in mathematics or science; however, the intellectual household environment likely fostered academic ambition.
primary_early_advantage_tags: intellectual family, elite university, precocious mathematical ability
evidence_summary: Shelah decided to become a mathematician at age 15 after discovering geometry, earning his B.Sc. from Tel Aviv University at 19 and his PhD from Hebrew University at 24 in 1969. His doctoral work on stable theories under Michael Rabin extended Morley's categoricity theorem and laid the foundation for classification theory in model theory. He immediately secured a lecturer position at Princeton, followed by an assistant professorship at UCLA. His father, Yonatan Ratosh, was a prominent Israeli poet, providing an intellectual but not mathematical family background.
starting_point: Born in Jerusalem in 1945 to Yonatan Ratosh, a prominent Israeli poet and political activist, providing an intellectual but not scientific family environment.
current_position: Professor of mathematics at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Distinguished Visiting Professor at Rutgers University; one of the most prolific mathematicians with over 1100 publications.

trajectory.event: Completed PhD on stable theories at Hebrew University and appointed lecturer at Princeton University.
Assistant professor at UCLA, then returned to Hebrew University as assistant professor.
Promoted to full professor at Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
Awarded the Erdős Prize in Mathematics by the Israel Mathematical Union.
Plenary speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Berkeley; appointed Distinguished Visiting Professor at Rutgers.
Awarded the Bolyai Prize for his monograph Cardinal Arithmetic.

name: Daniel Mojon
milestone_by_age_26: Completed medical school at age 25 in 1988, but this is a standard educational credential; his major contribution (inventing minimally invasive strabismus surgery) came in the late 1990s–2000s, well after age 26.

name: Zhores Alferov

name: Susi Susanti
milestone_by_age_26: Won the All England Open badminton title in 1990 at age 19, establishing herself as the dominant women's singles player of the early 1990s.
early_history_summary: Susi started badminton as a child in Tasikmalaya, trained daily by her father, a former regional player whose career ended with a knee injury. She practiced at her uncle's club PB Tunas for seven years before moving to Jakarta at 14 to join PB Jaya Raya under coach Liang Chiu Sia, training six days a week. She reached the All England final at 18 in 1989 and won it at 19 in 1990.
family_context_summary: Born in Tasikmalaya, West Java, to Risad Haditono and Purwo Banowati; father was a regional-level badminton player whose career was cut short by a knee injury.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a badminton enthusiast and former regional player who trained Susi daily from a young age, teaching footwork, stamina, and technique.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father-coach, daily training, elite club, national training center
evidence_summary: Susi Susanti was born in Tasikmalaya to a badminton-enthusiast family; her father, a former regional player whose career ended with a knee injury, trained her daily from a young age. She practiced at her uncle's club PB Tunas for seven years before moving to Jakarta at 14 to join PB Jaya Raya, where she trained under coach Liang Chiu Sia with a rigorous six-day-per-week schedule. At 18, she reached the All England final, and at 19 in 1990, she won the All England Open, establishing herself as the dominant women's singles player of the early 1990s.
starting_point: Born in Tasikmalaya, West Java, Indonesia to a badminton-enthusiast family; father was a former regional-level badminton player whose career was cut short by injury.
current_position: Chairperson of PB Jaya Raya Jakarta badminton club; married to fellow Olympic gold medalist Alan Budikusuma; owns badminton equipment company ASTEC.

trajectory.event: Won the All England Open badminton title, the oldest and most prestigious badminton tournament.
Won Olympic gold at Barcelona, becoming Indonesia's first-ever Olympic gold medalist.
Won the IBF World Championships singles title.
Won Olympic bronze at Atlanta and led Indonesia to Uber Cup victory.
Retired from competitive badminton after marriage.
Inducted into the BWF Hall of Fame.

name: Derek Muller
milestone_by_age_26: Completed a PhD in physics education research at the University of Sydney in 2008 at age 25–26; his major public milestone (launching Veritasium) came in 2011 at age 28–29.

name: Sébastien Loeb
milestone_by_age_26: Won the French Citroën Saxo Trophy Series title in 1999 at age 25, launching his professional rally career with the manufacturer that would carry him to a record nine WRC championships.
early_history_summary: Loeb competed in gymnastics from age 3, winning four Alsatian titles, before switching to rallying at 21 in 1995 with limited finances. He worked as an electrician while entering the Rallye Jeunes talent contest, was named most promising driver by Echappement magazine in 1997, and formed his enduring partnership with co-driver Daniel Elena the same year.
family_context_summary: Born in Haguenau, Alsace, the only child of Guy and Ingrid Loeb; father was a gymnast champion turned PE teacher who introduced Sébastien to gymnastics at age 3.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a gymnastics champion and later a PE teacher, providing athletic training from age 3 but no motorsport connections or financial support for racing.
primary_early_advantage_tags: gymnastics background, co-driver partnership, financial constraint, talent contest
evidence_summary: Loeb grew up in Haguenau, Alsace, the son of a gymnast champion turned PE teacher, and competed in gymnastics from age 3, winning multiple Alsatian titles. He switched to rallying at 21 in 1995 with limited financial resources, working as an electrician to fund his early career. He won the Rallye Jeunes regional selection and was named most promising driver by Echappement magazine in 1997. In 1999, at age 25, he won the French Citroën Saxo Trophy title, launching his path to becoming the greatest rally driver in history.
starting_point: Born in Haguenau, Alsace, France to Guy and Ingrid Loeb; father was a gymnast champion turned PE teacher who introduced him to gymnastics at age 3.
current_position: Active racing driver competing in World Rally-Raid Championship for Dacia; nine-time WRC champion; widely considered the greatest rally driver of all time.

trajectory.event: Won the French Citroën Saxo Trophy Series title, securing manufacturer backing.
Won the Junior World Rally Championship Super 1600 class.
Took maiden WRC win at Rallye Deutschland with Citroën.
Won first WRC drivers' world championship title.
Won ninth consecutive WRC title, a record, before retiring from full-time rallying.
Competing in Dakar Rally and World Rally-Raid Championship for Dacia.

name: Josef Musil
milestone_by_age_26: Won a World Championship silver medal with Czechoslovakia in 1952 at age 20, followed by European Championship gold in 1955 and World Championship gold in 1956, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Musil was born in the small village of Kostelní Lhota and moved to Prague in 1946 at age 14, where his volleyball talents were first noticed. He joined the Czechoslovakian national team at 19 and became a setter for Slavia Prague, known for his technical precision and artful setting rather than power.
family_context_summary: Born in the small village of Kostelní Lhota, Czechoslovakia; family moved to Prague in 1946 where his volleyball talents were first noticed.
primary_early_advantage_tags: national team, Slavia Prague, early talent identification
evidence_summary: Musil was born in the small village of Kostelní Lhota and moved to Prague in 1946 at age 14, where his volleyball talents were first noticed. He joined the Czechoslovakian national team at 19 and won a World Championship silver medal at 20 in 1952. As a setter for Slavia Prague, he was known for his technical precision rather than power. He went on to win World Championship golds in 1956 and 1966, European Championship golds in 1955 and 1958, and Olympic silver and bronze medals in 1964 and 1968.
starting_point: Born in the small village of Kostelní Lhota, Czechoslovakia; family moved to Prague in 1946 where his volleyball talents were first noticed.
current_position: Died on August 26, 2017 in Prague, Czech Republic at age 85; final role: retired volleyball player and coach, inducted into International Volleyball Hall of Fame in 2004.

trajectory.event: Won World Championship silver medal with Czechoslovakia in Moscow.
Won European Championship gold medal with Czechoslovakia.
Won World Championship gold medal in Paris.
Won second European Championship gold medal on home soil in Czechoslovakia.
Won Olympic silver medal at the Tokyo Games.
Won World Championship gold on home soil in Czechoslovakia.
Won Olympic bronze medal at the Mexico City Games.
Died in Prague, Czech Republic.

name: Kateryna Serebrianska
milestone_by_age_26: Won the rope title at the 1993 World Championships in Alicante at age 16, and achieved a historic sweep of all four event finals at the 1994 World Championships in Paris, one of only two gymnasts ever to do so.
early_history_summary: Serebrianska started rhythmic gymnastics at age 4 in 1982, coached by her mother Liubov at the Gratsia club in Simferopol, which was directed by her father Oleg. She trained up to 8 hours per day, 6 days per week, and later moved to Kyiv to train at the elite Deriugina School, refining her technique across all five apparatus.
family_context_summary: Born in Simferopol, Ukrainian SSR; father Oleg was a football player (USSR champion with Dnipro in 1985) and later director of the Gratsia gymnastics club; mother Liubov was a gymnastics coach and former gymnast who trained alongside Lyudmila Turishcheva.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were sports professionals: father a football champion and sports club director, mother a gymnast-turned-coach who became Serebrianska's first trainer at age 4.
primary_early_advantage_tags: mother-coach, sports family, elite training school, early start
evidence_summary: Serebrianska started rhythmic gymnastics at age 4 in 1982, coached by her mother Liubov at the Gratsia club in Simferopol, which was directed by her father Oleg, a former USSR football champion. She trained up to 8 hours per day, 6 days per week, and moved to Kyiv to train at the elite Deriugina School. At 16, she won the rope title at the 1993 World Championships, and at 17, she achieved a historic sweep of all four event finals at the 1994 World Championships, one of only two gymnasts ever to do so.
starting_point: Born in Simferopol, Ukrainian SSR to a sports family; father was a USSR football champion and sports club director, mother was a gymnast-turned-coach.
current_position: Runs Serebrianska Group wellness businesses in Ukraine; studying nutrition therapy at CNM College of Naturopathic Medicine in London; retired from gymnastics in 1998.

trajectory.event: Won rope title at the World Championships in Alicante, Spain.
Swept all four event finals at the World Championships in Paris, one of only two gymnasts ever to achieve this.
Tied for World All-around champion at the World Championships in Vienna.
Won Olympic gold medal at Atlanta and European All-around champion.
Retired from competitive rhythmic gymnastics.

name: Félix Rodríguez
milestone_by_age_26: Participated in the CIA-supported Bay of Pigs Invasion in April 1961 at age 19 as a Brigade 2506 operative, having infiltrated Cuba to gather intelligence before the operation.
early_history_summary: Rodríguez was born into a family of landowners in Havana and sent to the Perkiomen School in Pennsylvania in 1954. After Castro's revolution, he joined the CIA-supported Brigade 2506 in Guatemala in September 1960 at age 19, received military training, and clandestinely entered Cuba before the failed Bay of Pigs Invasion.
family_context_summary: Born in Havana, Cuba, to a family of landowners; his uncle served as Minister of Public Works under Fulgencio Batista's government.
primary_early_advantage_tags: family wealth, political connections, CIA training, exile network
evidence_summary: Rodríguez was born into a family of landowners in Havana, Cuba, with his uncle serving as Minister of Public Works under Batista. Sent to the Perkiomen School in Pennsylvania in 1954, he joined the CIA-supported Brigade 2506 in September 1960 at age 19 and was trained in Guatemala. He infiltrated Cuba before the failed Bay of Pigs Invasion in April 1961, gathering critical intelligence. His family's wealth and connections enabled his US education and entry into the CIA-trained exile force.
starting_point: Born in Havana, Cuba to a family of landowners; uncle was Minister of Public Works under Batista; sent to boarding school in Pennsylvania in 1954.
current_position: Retired CIA paramilitary officer, age 84; resides in Miami; speaks at military bases and universities about his covert operations career.

trajectory.event: Participated in the Bay of Pigs Invasion as a CIA-trained Brigade 2506 operative after infiltrating Cuba.
Led the CIA team that captured Che Guevara in Bolivia.
Retired from the CIA.
Became involved in the Iran-Contra affair, managing illegal Contra re-supply operations in Nicaragua.
Retired and living in Miami; speaks at military bases and universities about his career.
